steps.text: Bring water and sugar to a boil in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Add cranberries, apples, cider vinegar, raisins, cinnamon, ginger, allspice, and cloves. Return to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer gently, stirring often, for 10 minutes.
Pour mixture into a mixing bowl.
Place plastic wrap directly on the surface of the fruit. Let cool to room temperature before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Cranberry Chutney
raw_recipe.description: This cranberry chutney with apples, raisins, and spices is a deliciously fruity alternative to regular cranberry sauce on your holiday table.

review.reviewBody: Absolutely the best!! I made it for thanksgiving. I had a fresh orange on hand, so I zested it and added, and it made a difference (I love orange peel), but it would have still be great without it, as another user said. I did cut down the vinegar to 2TBsp as recommended by most. (I doubled the recipe and used 1/4 cup). I was not sure which apples to use, so I asked someone, and they recommended MacIntosh (they break down better)...worked well. Amazing recipe! I loved it! This will be my standard cranberry sauce from now on. Thank you very much!!! Those who did not try it because they dont like cranberries have no idea what they are missing!
I love cranberry chutney. It's not winter without it. I cut the sugar in half and add fresh squeezed OJ instead of water. I also add in some orange zest. Superb!

I made a couple changes. As others had said there was a pronounced vinegar taste, I only added 1 1/2 T. I added slightly less apples and raisins, and added the zest of one orange plus a couple T of freshly squeezed orange juice. After it simmered a little while, I mashed some of the chutney so it would have a more saucy texture, but left chunks in as well.

The anti-vinegar people here are missing the point. This is cranberry chutney, not Ocean Spray canned cranberry jelly. There are most likely other recipes here like the way I make it, but, here I go:

Saute 1/2 cup of onion for a while, throw in some garlic when the onion is soft, then proceed with the recipe. You can do without the apples and raisins as far as I'm concerned. I used 3/4 c. packed brown sugar and rice wine vinegar. I like adding orange jest. I just used 1 tsp. of ground ginger, instead of all the other spices. Grated fresh ginger would be very good. In fact, if you want it really orange-y, replace the water with orange juice.

I've made this recipe twice since Thanksgiving, as others suggested I used less vinegar. I only used 1 TB of red wine vinegar, 1/4 tea of balsamic vinegar, 1 tea of pumpkin spice & 1 granny smith apple cut in small pieces. It took longer to cook then 10 minutes but it was worth the wait, this recipe is a keeper :-)

After reading what others had to say about this recipe, I made some variations to the recipe, all else remaining the same: 3/4 c white sugar, 1/2 c light brown sugar, 2-3 fuji apples, 2 tbsp cider vinegar, omitted the raisins, cooked it for 25-30 min to reach the thick consistency I was looking for, and then gently mashed the apples. I found that if you eat it right after making it while it's still warm, it's a little more tart and "vinegary," but if you refrigerate it over night, it lessens the tartness and vinegar element so it's just right!

I used 2 tab. cider vinegar, added 1/4 c. each of diced apple,celery and onion.
came out tart, chunky texture, and a hit at my Thanksgiving table!

I didn't have cranberries and didn't want to go to the store so I used the canned whole berry stuff. I chopped up a Granny Smith apple, boiled it in a small amount of water until it was soft, then added the raisins, spices, a couple of Tbls of vinegar and cranberry sauce. No sugar needed, the cranberry sauce already has plenty. Without anything to compare against, I find it delicious. I wil try it with fresh cranberries next time tho, so I can control the sugar

This is a must have on all my holiday tables. The only substitute I make is the sugar, as I follow a sugar free lifestyle. The vinegar seemed to be a lot to me the first couple times, but I trusted the recipe. The longer it sits, the more amazing it is, exactly as written. I like to make ahead a day or two, but six hours minimum works well. I have added orange peel and crushed pecans in the past, to rave reviews. It's absolutely wonderful as written.

Great recipe. I did though make a couple of modifications. Based on other reviews I reduced the cider vinegar to 1/4 cup (2 tablespoons would have been too little). I also used pumpkin pie spice instead of ground cloves. And I added 1/4 cup of diced raw walnuts. The flavor is killer. I've never made chutney before and I will never buy it again! Next time I will try it with the full amount of vinegar.

This was very good! So good I brought it to Thanksgiving and it was all eaten or taken home in to go containers! So I'll have to make it again. I did sub ground cloves because they didn't process in my food processor so I pulled out the whole cloves that were left and used a bit of nutmeg, but it was a total hit! Thanks again!!

It was easy to make and made the kitchen smell wonderful while it was cooking. The finished sauce was a sweet and tangy, chunky sauce, with warm winter spices, similar to apple butter. So much better than regular cranberry sauce!
Great recipe and flavors. I did end up, swapping out the sugar for date paste. Just cooked down one cup of pitted dates and replaced them with the sugar and the raisins.

This came together easily. All I needed to buy were the cranberries. I followed the recipe exactly. It has a *snappy* flavor due to the delicious seasonal spices. I made the chutney to use in a brie/chutney/puff pastry appetizer I'm bringing to a dinner Thanksgiving. This made enough to fill two recycled jelly jars.
My substitute: No raisins (family dislike lol) 1 cup Saskatoons 3/4 diced dates 1/8 tsp cumin Passed the holiday crew with flying colours!!
Amazing chutney! Made it for a Thanksgiving dinner and my great aunt couldn't stop talking about it!
I halved the acv, and all I had was Pumpkin Spice and I added more cinnamon. Zero left over. I didn't peel the apple, didn't seem to matter. I'll definitely make it again.

I did the recipe exactly as written for Thanksgiving. It was terrific. I did it for a potluck today and used leftover Proseco instead of ACV and cut the sugar in half. It was excellent and very well received. This is a wonderful recipe.
This is the first time i tried this. this is excellent! My son in-laws dad made this. I will make it also. i would give it 6 stars if I could He left out the ginger and thats ok with me.
I’ve been making this stuff for years. Reduced the vinegar by half too. Love it.
